stem:
Falguni spins a round steel plate about its centre and also folds it along diameters through that centre.

Which claim correctly explains why the circle is a special limiting case for symmetry?

options.text: The plate matches itself after any turn about its centre, and every diameter is a line of symmetry.
Symmetry holds for the plate only when the fold misses the centre.
The centre is produced by already knowing the plate has infinitely many symmetries.
The plate has exactly four symmetry lines, matching a square.

teacher.key_rationale: Any rotation about the centre and every diameter as a mirror make the circle a limiting case. Requiring folds that miss the centre omits the centre condition. Saying the centre is produced by knowing infinite symmetries reverses the relation. Limiting to four lines over-scopes like a square.
